name: Question 7
problem:
Consider the system ${x}^{′}(t)=Ax(t),$ where $A$ is a constant $2\times 2$ matrix. Let $Φ(t)$ be a fundamental matrix for this system. A derivation showing that $Φ(t)$ is invertible for all $t$ is given below.

$\text{L1}:\,$ Let ${x}_{1}(t)$ and ${x}_{2}(t)$ be the columns of $Φ(t)$

$\text{L2}:\,$ ${x}_{1}(t)$ and ${x}_{2}(t)$ are linearly independent for all $t$

$\text{L3}:\,$ $det(Φ(t))\ne 0$ for all $t$

$\text{L4}:\,$ $Φ(t)$ is invertible for all $t$

Select the correct options in the following reasoning.

$\,$ Line $\text{L2}$ follows from $\text{L1}$ by the {{field-1}}.

$\,$ Line $\text{L3}$ follows from line $\text{L2}$ by {{field-2}}.

$\,$ Line $\text{L4}$ follows from line {{field-3}} by the properties of invertible matrices.

Consider the system x′(t)=Ax(t), where A is a constant 2×2 matrix. Let Φ(t) be a fundamental matrix for this system. A derivation showing that Φ(t) is invertible for all t is given below.

L1: Let x1(t) and x2(t) be the columns of Φ(t)

L2: x1(t) and x2(t) are linearly independent for all t

L3: det(Φ(t))≠0 for all t

L4: Φ(t) is invertible for all t

Select the correct options in the following reasoning.

Line L2 follows from L1 by the
 
definition of a fundamental matrix
properties of invertible matrices
properties of diagonalizable matrices
definition of matrix multiplication
.

Line L3 follows from line L2 by
 
the properties of determinants
the zero factor theorem
integrating the given system
substituting Φ′=AΦ
.

Line L4 follows from line
 
L3
L1
L4
L2
by the properties of invertible matrices.
